newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Freed Hamas leader says Israel might kill him.
newsitem.headline: Freed Hamas leader says Israel might kill him.

text.p: Freed Palestinian Hamas political leader Musa Abu Marzook said in remarks published on Saturday that Israel might try to assassinate him.
"My assassination by Israel is a probability," Abu Marzook told Kuwait's al-Rai al-Aam in Jordan after his return this week from nearly two years detention in a New York jail.
His deportation followed Israel's decision to drop an extradition demand despite claims that he was involved in a wave of attacks against Israelis between 1990 and 1994.

"I do not discount Israel's planning of something similar to Fathi Shqaqi's assassination" in 1995 in Malta, Abu Marzook said. The Palestinian militant group Islamic Jihad accused the Israeli intelligence Mossad of killing its leader, Fathi Shqaqi.
Abu Marzook said that the United States had dropped earlier demands to restrict his political activity or movement.
"I am free in my movements and in what I do and say but in the same time I abide by Jordanian laws," he added.
Jordan has said that it was not putting constraints on his activities but said he would be subject to Jordanian law. Diplomats expect his movements to be be closely monitored.
